alerts.title: Carbamazepine significantly reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. Carbamazepine was started 2 weeks ago, and the viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This timeline strongly supports a drug interaction causing subtherapeutic DTG concentrations. The guideline recommends using valproic acid instead of carbamazepine. The patient is already on sodium valproate, so carbamazepine may have been added unnecessarily or could be replaced by optimizing valproate.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid or an alternative anti-epileptic that does not reduce DTG levels. Repeat viral load after the change.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with elevated level and hyponatremia
alerts.message: Carbamazepine level is 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12). Patient has nystagmus, ataxia, and tremor—classic carbamazepine neurotoxicity. Hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also a known carbamazepine adverse effect. ALT 68 U/L may reflect carbamazepine hepatotoxicity, though TDF can also elevate transaminases. The clinician plans dose reduction, which is appropriate. Concurrent valproate may compound CNS toxicity and hepatotoxicity. Close monitoring of sodium, LFTs, and carbamazepine levels is essential.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level, and monitor sodium, LFTs, and neurologic symptoms. Consider neurology review for dual antiepileptic therapy.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires repeat testing
alerts.message: Guidelines state virological monitoring indicates treatment failure and need for regimen switch. Viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL. While the DTG–carbamazepine interaction is the likely cause, a single detectable result may represent a viral blip. Guidelines support repeat viral load to confirm before switching therapy. The clinician's plan does not include a repeat viral load or enhanced adherence assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat viral load after addressing the carbamazepine interaction. If still detectable, assess adherence and consider resistance testing before regimen switch.
